p: when he had ended all his: Christ admonishes the Jews that for their obstinacy and rebellion he will go to the Gentiles, by setting before them the example of the centurion.
And it came to pass the: Christ openly affirms his power over death.
Nain: Nain is the name of a town in Galilee which was situated on the other side of the Kishon, which runs into the sea of Galilee.
And the disciples of John shewed: John sends from the prison his unbelieving disciples to be confirmed by Christ himself.
in that same hour he cured: When John's disciples came to Christ.

And when the messengers of John: That which the prophets showed long before, John shows presently: and Christ himself presents it daily unto us in the gospel, but for the most part in vain, because many seek nothing else than foolish toys and vain glory.
justified God: Said that he was just, good, faithful and merciful.
against themselves: To their own hurt.
And the Lord said: Whatever manner God uses in offering us the gospel, most men bring offences upon themselves: yet nevertheless a Church is gathered together.

And one of the Pharisees desired: Proud men deprive themselves of the benefits of the presence of Christ, even when he is at home with them in their houses; and these benefits the humble and base enjoy.
Now when the Pharisee which had: Rashness is the companion of pride.
for she is a sinner: The Pharisee respects the law, which holds that those who touch the defiled are defiled.
And Jesus answering said unto him: To love Christ is a sure and perpetual witness of the remission of sins.

for she loved much: That is, says Theophylact, she has shown her faith abundantly: and Basil in his "Sermon of Baptism" says, "He that owes much has much forgiven him, that he may love much more". And therefore Christ's saying is so plain in light of this that it is a wonder to see the enemies of the truth so badly distort and misinterpret this place in such a thorough manner in order to establish their meritorious works: for the greater sum a man has forgiven him, the more he loves him that has been so gracious to him. And this woman shows by deeds of love how great the benefit was she had received: and therefore the charity that is here spoken of is not to be taken as the cause of her forgiveness, but as a sign of it: for Christ does not say as the Pharisees did that she was a sinner, but bears her witness that the sins of her past life are forgiven her.
go in peace: He confirms with a blessing the benefit which he had bestowed.
